posts.text: Strategic Energy Map is live: a free, ad-free map of global oil and gas infrastructure. Chokepoint ship traffic, facility status, pump prices and what-if scenarios, updated daily with every item sourced.
Diesel prices since the Strait of Hormuz closed: US +71%, EU average +40%, UK +38% (week of 21 Sep vs week of 23 Feb).
posts.alt: Bar chart of the change in diesel prices since the week of 23 February 2026 for the US, UK, EU average, Germany, France, Italy, Spain, the Netherlands and Poland.

posts.text: 2 new developments today: Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline has recovered to ~3.5 million b/d (about half capacity), and Kpler data show Hormuz crude exports averaging 7.4 million b/d in September (reported). Brent held near $105/bbl.

About 19.9 million b/d of oil crossed the Strait of Hormuz before the war. Pipelines around it had only ~3.5 million b/d of spare capacity (IEA, low estimate), leaving ~16.4 million b/d with no alternative route.
posts.alt: Bar chart, million barrels a day: oil through the Strait of Hormuz before the war 19.9; spare pipeline capacity around it 3.5; no alternative route 16.4.

posts.text: Saudi Arabia's Yanbu export terminal shows a 'major operational recovery' (Kpler satellite imagery), with Strait of Hormuz flows at a 13.2 million b/d 7-day average — about 77% of pre-war (reported). Brent $97/bbl, WTI $90/bbl as of 30 Sep.
Kpler and satellite imagery show a 'major operational recovery' at Saudi Arabia's Yanbu terminal. Strait of Hormuz flows are now a 13.2 million b/d 7-day average — about 77% of pre-war (reported).

Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline runs ~1,200 km from Abqaiq to Yanbu, the kingdom's main Hormuz-bypass route. Shut by drone strikes on 11 Sep, it's back to about 3.5 million b/d — half its 7 million b/d capacity.

Before the 2026 crisis, about 23.2 million b/d of oil moved through the Strait of Malacca and 19.9 million b/d through Hormuz, each about a fifth of world demand. Suez, Bab el-Mandeb and the other chokepoints carried far less.
posts.alt: Bar chart of oil flows before the 2026 crisis, million barrels a day: Strait of Malacca 23.2, Strait of Hormuz 19.9, Suez Canal 4.9, Bab el-Mandeb 4.2, Turkish Straits 3.7, Panama Canal 2.3.

posts.text: JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs estimate Middle East crude flows are near pre-war levels, while UKMTO's delayed reports reveal 3 more Hormuz tanker attacks. Brent $99.74/bbl, WTI $91.45/bbl as of 1 Oct.

JPMorgan estimates Mideast crude shipments at 17.5 million b/d, 98% of pre-war, Hormuz near 13 million b/d. Goldman Sachs puts Gulf exports at 23.3 million b/d in September, matching 2025 — adapting to risk, not safer.

UKMTO disclosed 3 more Hormuz tanker attacks via delayed warnings, with vessel identities, damage and casualties still unconfirmed days later — a widening gap in incident reporting even as overall traffic recovers.

Aramco's Abqaiq plant stabilises up to 7 million b/d of crude, over half of Saudi output, before export on the East-West pipeline. Drones from Iraq hit it 27 Jul 2026; repair status isn't confirmed since.

AIS-tracked tanker traffic through Hormuz averaged 1.3/day in the week to 27 Sep, 97% below baseline — many sail dark, so broader tracking shows higher flows. Turkish Straits -48%, Bab el-Mandeb -22%.
posts.alt: Bar chart of 7-day average tanker transits vs pre-crisis baseline, percent change: Strait of Hormuz -97% (1.3/day), Turkish Straits -48% (11.7/day), Bab el-Mandeb -22% (9.4/day), Strait of Malacca -17% (70.0/day), Panama Canal -10% (11.7/day), Suez Canal -4% (15.0/day).

posts.text: US Treasury sanctioned Iran's carmakers and railways on 1 Oct, targeting overland oil routes used since the Hormuz blockade; Washington pressed Germany and France on diesel reserves. Brent $99.81, WTI $89.36 on 2 Oct.
US Treasury sanctions targeted Iran Khodro and Saipa, the state railway and a freight operator, saying Tehran has shifted oil and other goods to road and rail since the Hormuz blockade tightened.

The US pressed Germany and France to release more diesel reserves, saying both drew down only a fraction of their IEA pledge. Germany won't release 15 million barrels; France released none (reported).

Egypt's Suez Canal carries ~5-6 million b/d of oil and products, plus cargo worth ~12% of global trade. Houthi attacks diverted over half its traffic around the Cape since late 2023; transits were ~36% below normal in August.

UKMTO now counts six Hormuz tanker strikes since 28 Sep, and officials say Saudi Arabia is preparing an offensive to retake Bab el-Mandeb from the Houthis. Brent held near $100 (2 Oct); US diesel $6.38/gal, week of 28 Sep.

Six officials say Saudi Arabia is preparing a Yemeni-led offensive, backed by Saudi air power, to retake Bab el-Mandeb from Houthi control. Timing ranges from within a week to after the US midterms (reported).
UKMTO's delayed disclosures now put at six the number of vessels struck in the Strait of Hormuz since 28 September. No casualties were reported and responsibility wasn't attributed.

The UK sanctioned eight more vessels tied to Russia's shadow fleet and LNG exports, including five named LNG carriers, and has now sanctioned nearly 600 tankers moving Russian energy around Western restrictions.
Bab el-Mandeb, between Yemen and Djibouti, normally carries about 6-7 million b/d of oil toward Suez. Houthi attacks have left it disrupted since 20 July, transits still ~15% below pre-ban levels.
Brent fell to $102.25, WTI to $91.11 on Oct 2 as G7 agreed to release 100m barrels of reserves. Reuters/AFP saw a fire at Aramco's Riyadh refinery on Oct 3.

The Strait of Hormuz is the top oil chokepoint, normally ~20m b/d of crude and a fifth of LNG trade. Closed to normal traffic since Feb 28; flows averaged 13.2 mb/d through Sep 29, ~77% of pre-war levels, under escort.
UKMTO logged a seventh Hormuz tanker struck in a week (no casualties) as Brent ticked up to $102.80 and WTI held near $90.63. TTF gas eased to €74.43/MWh.

UKMTO: an unknown projectile hit tanker Lipsi's engine room in the Strait of Hormuz on Oct 4, leaving it disabled. Crew safe, no environmental impact — at least the seventh vessel hit there since late Sep.
The CPC pipeline moves Kazakh crude 1,510 km from Tengiz to Russia's Novorossiysk terminal, capacity ~1.4m b/d — most of Kazakhstan's oil exports, and a repeated target in the Black Sea war.
Brent fell to $97.95 and WTI to $87.32, a third straight drop, as Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline topped 80% capacity and forces reported gains toward Bab el-Mandeb while Hormuz stays closed.

Riyadh Refinery is Aramco's only refinery serving the Saudi capital: 126,000 b/d, fed by the East-West pipeline, not a coastal terminal. Disrupted since an Oct 3 fire Houthis claimed as a strike (unconfirmed).
Brent rebounded to $101.90 and WTI to $89.98, snapping three days of declines, as a new Hormuz tanker strike injured a dozen seafarers and Iran's oil exports near zero under the US blockade.

Ras Laffan, Qatar's LNG export complex, ships ~77 million tonnes a year with no pipeline bypass of Hormuz. Qatar just parked a dozen empty carriers in the Gulf, hinting it may try to raise exports despite the attack risk.

Brent jumped to $105.20 and WTI to $92.69, up about 5%, as Hurricane Isaias forced US Gulf producers to shut in about a quarter of output and Hormuz tanker attacks hit their highest weekly total since the war began.

Qatar and Iran share the world's largest gas field: Qatar's North Field feeds its LNG exports, Iran's South Pars still limited by Israel's March strike. Qatar just parked a dozen empty LNG carriers in the Gulf.

Trump: the US won't strike Iran before November's midterms. Oil eased to Brent $102.81, WTI $90.56, even as Gulf of Mexico shut-ins hit 63% of output ahead of Hurricane Isaias, and a tanker was struck off Qatar, west of Hormuz.

A chemical tanker was struck by projectiles off Qatar on Oct 7, UKMTO said — about 51 nautical miles offshore, well west of the usual Strait of Hormuz attack cluster. No party has claimed responsibility.
Gulf-to-Asia supertanker rates hit a record near $1.4 million a day, Signal Ocean data showed, up about 540% since before the war, as owners chase Hormuz-transit fees and shuttle-system demand.
The UAE's Hormuz insurance: the Habshan-Fujairah pipeline moves Abu Dhabi crude 370km to the Gulf of Oman, bypassing the strait — about 1.5 million b/d, mirroring Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline.

Trump announced a Russia-US diesel deal, with Treasury easing sanctions on Russia's energy sector (reported); no diesel has shipped yet. Brent $102.81, WTI $90.56. Gulf of Mexico shut-ins hit 71.5% of output ahead of Hurricane Isaias.

Russia's refining war: Rosneft's Tuapse refinery on the Black Sea (~240,000 b/d) has been offline since April drone strikes; Ukraine struck Gazprom Neft's Omsk refinery, Russia's largest, for a second time on Oct 8.

Hurricane Isaias weakened to post-tropical after landfall near Destin, Fla. Gulf shut-ins eased to about 69% as DOE OK'd a 4M-barrel SPR exchange for Exxon, BP. Brent $102.81; Hormuz exports ~8.5 mb/d, ~40% below pre-war.

The Cape of Good Hope isn't a chokepoint, it's the escape valve: ships skip Suez and Bab el-Mandeb, adding ~3,500 nautical miles and 10-14 days around Africa. In heavy use since Houthi attacks began in 2023.

Iran's security chief called the US Hormuz-reopening response insufficient; two more tankers were hit by projectiles in the strait over the weekend (Oct 10-11). Brent $105.60/bbl (+2.7% w/w); US diesel $6.20/gal (-2.9% w/w).

The Panama-flagged VLCC GEM NO.2 was hit by an unidentified projectile on Oct 9 about 13 nm west of Al Jazeera, UAE, outside the usual Hormuz attack cluster. Fire extinguished; no group claimed responsibility.
Diesel prices since the Strait of Hormuz closed: US +63%, EU average +35%, UK +41% (week of Oct 5 vs week of Feb 23).

posts.text: UKMTO and JMIC reports disclosed the Oct 11 Hormuz toll was six vessels, not two — the highest single-day total since the war began. Brent $104.64/bbl (-0.9% d/d); US diesel $6.20/gal (week of Oct 5).

SUMED pipeline, jointly owned by Egypt and four Gulf states, runs 320 km from the Red Sea to the Mediterranean — a bypass for tankers too large for the Suez Canal. Nameplate capacity: 2.5 million b/d, commissioned 1977.

Brent rose to about $106.55/bbl and WTI to $95.23 as supertankers avoid the Fujairah hub near Hormuz (Bloomberg tanker-tracking data) and Saudi Arabia traded strikes with Yemen's Houthis. US diesel $6.20/gal (week of Oct 5).
A Houthi strike on Riyadh airport killed at least 13 over the weekend, the deadliest attack on Saudi Arabia in a decade, as the Saudi-Houthi conflict escalates.
Saudi Arabia is studying raising East-West pipeline capacity from 5.8 to as much as 10 million b/d within 2-3 years, plus a gas-line conversion for 1.2 million b/d more crude, to bypass Hormuz.

Aramco's Jazan refinery on Saudi Arabia's Red Sea coast, the kingdom's refinery closest to Yemen, has been shut since Houthi strikes in late July knocked out its power complex and tank farm. Nameplate capacity: 400,000 b/d.

Houthi missiles and drones struck Aramco's Dhahran HQ overnight Oct 13, sparking a fire across several floors; Riyadh's airport stays closed through Oct 17. Brent eased to $104.63/bbl, US diesel $6.18/gal (week of Oct 12).

Two more ships went down near Hormuz: container ship GFS Pride sank Oct 13 (21 crew safe), and bulk carrier Cape Dao, hit Sep 23, has now sunk too. A security firm found no evidence for Iran's mine claim on the Pride.
Drones hit two cargo ships off Bulgaria's coast Oct 13: HS Dignity sank, 11 crew missing; Chelsea 3 caught fire but stayed afloat. Bulgaria blamed Russia; Moscow didn't confirm it.
Tanker transits (AIS-visible) fell further this week: Hormuz down to 0.6 ships/day, 99% below baseline, as many sail dark. Bosporus -36%, Bab el-Mandeb -29%, Panama -27%, Malacca -12%; Suez +9%.
posts.alt: Bar chart of 7-day average tanker transits vs pre-crisis baseline, percent change, week ending Oct 11: Strait of Hormuz -99% (0.6/day), Bosporus Strait -36% (14.6/day), Bab el-Mandeb -29% (8.6/day), Panama Canal -27% (9.4/day), Strait of Malacca -12% (74.9/day), Suez Canal +9% (17.0/day).

posts.text: JMIC counted just ~30 US-facilitated transits a day through Hormuz over Oct 11-14, about a fifth of the pre-war rate; the IMO puts the war's toll at 113 confirmed incidents, 24 seafarer deaths. Brent $105.91/bbl, US diesel $6.18/gal (week of Oct 12).
Drones hit tankers Wine Trader and Yara J off Romania's Black Sea coast Oct 15; 7 of Wine Trader's 12 crew are missing. A NATO official told Reuters the drones appeared Russian-made (unconfirmed).
The Trump administration may ease sanctions on tankers that carried Russian, Iranian or Venezuelan oil, Reuters reported, to relieve record freight rates squeezing Gulf and US crude exports.

Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline runs about 1,200 km from Abqaiq to Yanbu on the Red Sea, bypassing Hormuz entirely. Capacity: 7 million b/d. Aramco is now in talks to formalize long-term shuttle contracts on it.

UKMTO says most Hormuz-area attacks go unreported, counting only 42 AIS-tracked transits this week against the US's claimed 400. New data show Iran shipping LPG and jet fuel past the blockade since July. Brent is near $110/bbl, up from $106 yesterday.
The IEA agreed to speed up about 100 million barrels of emergency releases, including over 20 million barrels of diesel, citing the Hormuz crisis and a shortage it warned could last into 2027.
Gulf-to-China supertanker rates eased about 8% week on week to 776 Worldscale, down from a record 841, as Middle East demand cooled after fresh attacks. Rates stay near record highs.
Aramco's Abqaiq plant stabilizes most Eastern Province crude before export, with about 7 million bpd of capacity. A 2019 drone strike once knocked it offline, cutting roughly 5% of global oil supply.

Two tankers were struck northeast of Saudi Arabia's al-Jubail on Oct 16, outside Hormuz, UKMTO said; Iran separately claimed the ships hit mines (unverified). Brent held near $110/bbl over the weekend, up from $72.48 pre-crisis.

Vitol's Asia head said rising Hormuz crude flows won't fix a ship-fuel-oil shortage (reported). Gulf fuel-oil exports are down ~800,000 tons/month; Singapore bunker prices hit their highest since April.

Saudi Arabia's Ras al-Ju'aymah terminal took a surge in crude loadings after the Sep 10 pipeline attack: tankers loaded ~12 million barrels there Sep 21. It's Aramco's main LPG point, halted since Feb 23.

Iran repeated its offer to reopen Hormuz within 7 days if the US meets its conditions; Turkey said it will take diesel under the Russia-US deal. Brent eased to $108/bbl while EU gas (TTF) hit a fresh 2026 high of €89.56/MWh.

Turkey will take some of the diesel Russia is supplying under the Trump-Putin deal, Energy Minister Alparslan Bayraktar said, calling it important for Turkey's energy security after Russia curtailed exports.
Romanian F-16s shot down two drones over Black Sea waters on Oct 17, days after drone strikes hit two tankers near Ukraine's Sulina Canal, leaving seven crew still missing.

Hormuz is only ~21 km wide at its narrowest and normally carries about a fifth of world oil, near 20 million b/d. Closed since February; PortWatch tanker transits are down ~99% from pre-crisis levels.

Iran's oil terminals have sat idle since late August, the longest stretch of the war, as the US eases sanctions on 'dark fleet' tankers. Brent rose to about $111.50/bbl; UKMTO logged 25 Hormuz-area ship attacks in early October, vs 18 in September.

Brent eased to $110.74, off Monday's 5-month high, as Houthis claim (unverified) fresh strikes on Aramco's Yanbu site and the Shaybah field. Kpler data show Mideast oil flows, incl. Hormuz bypass routes, now match pre-war levels.
Kpler data show total Mideast oil flows -- Hormuz, Gulf of Oman transfers, Fujairah and Red Sea exports -- topped 24.5M b/d in the week to Oct 18, edging above the pre-war baseline (reported).

Aramco's Riyadh Refinery is the only major refinery serving the Saudi capital: about 126,000 b/d via the East-West Pipeline, not a coastal terminal. Disrupted since a Houthi strike claim sparked a fire on Oct 3.

UKMTO says ship attacks near the Arabian Peninsula have topped 32 in October, already double September's 16, even as Mideast oil flows hold near pre-war levels. Brent hit a fresh 5-month high near $112/bbl.
UKMTO has recorded 32 attacks on commercial vessels near the Arabian Peninsula so far in October, already double September's 16. Most ships in the area now sail with tracking off, it says.

Tanker transits (AIS-visible) stayed near rock bottom this week: Hormuz still 0.6 ships/day, 99% below baseline, as most sail dark. Turkish Straits -36%, Bab el-Mandeb -18%, Malacca -16%; Suez +2%, Panama flat.
posts.alt: Bar chart of 7-day average tanker transits vs pre-crisis baseline, percent change, week ending Oct 18: Strait of Hormuz -99% (0.6/day), Turkish Straits -36% (14.4/day), Bab el-Mandeb -18% (10.0/day), Strait of Malacca -16% (71.4/day), Panama Canal +0% (13.0/day), Suez Canal +2% (15.9/day).

posts.text: A Houthi drone strike near Aramco's Shaybah oilfield killed two contractors on Oct 21; Saudi Arabia's ministry says operations were unaffected. Brent hit $114.55/bbl, highest since May, up roughly 8% on the week. US diesel: $6.28/gal.
The US State Department ordered non-emergency diplomats and their families to leave Saudi Arabia on Oct 21, citing escalating Houthi attacks on civilian targets including Riyadh's main airport.

Brent settled at $116.72 on Oct 23, highest since April, on reports the US and Israel are planning renewed Iran strikes after the Nov 3 midterms. US diesel is $6.28/gal (+$0.10 w/w); Gulf oil flows hold near pre-war levels despite Hormuz attacks.
QatarEnergy signed a deal for up to 4 million tonnes a year of US LNG from Cheniere, 2031-2054, giving it supply outside the Gulf after Iran's strikes knocked out 17% of its Ras Laffan LNG capacity.

The US Treasury sanctioned a Greek law firm, two shipping agents and nine vessels for moving Iranian oil, petrochemicals and steel past sanctions, part of its Economic Outcast campaign against Tehran's shadow fleet.

The UAE's Habshan-Fujairah pipeline moves up to 1.8 million b/d of crude 370km from Abu Dhabi to Fujairah, letting ADNOC bypass Hormuz. It now anchors the shuttle system moving most Gulf crude past the strait.
An oil leak off the UAE coast shut beaches in three emirates. The IEA says Gulf-to-Asia shipping now costs over $37/barrel, 5x pre-war. Brent holds near $117/bbl. US diesel: $6.28/gal.
The IEA says shipping crude from the Gulf to Asia now costs over $37/barrel, more than 5x pre-war levels, as bypass pipelines and Gulf of Oman ship-to-ship transfers keep oil moving at a steep price.
Tanker rates for the US Gulf Coast-to-China route hit nearly $60 million by late October, up from under $8 million before the war. November US crude orders for Asia are down about 50% (Vortexa).

Saudi Arabia's SAMREF refinery at Yanbu, an Aramco-ExxonMobil JV, processes about 400,000 b/d via the East-West pipeline. Yanbu is the kingdom's main Hormuz-bypass outlet, now in Houthi attacks' path.

Hormuz transits fell to about a quarter of normal over Oct 22-24 (JMIC); roughly 492 ships now wait outside the strait. Houthi missiles again targeted Yanbu and Riyadh over the weekend. Brent holds near $116.72/bbl; US diesel: $6.28/gal.
JMIC counted just 101 Hormuz transits over Oct 22-24, about a quarter of the ~138/day pre-war baseline. Bab el-Mandeb traffic is also down, to about 58 transits over the same three days.
Saudi-led air defenses intercepted Houthi missiles toward Yanbu and Taif on Oct 24, then Riyadh and Khamis Mushait air base on Oct 25. No damage to Aramco facilities was reported.
Diesel prices since the Strait of Hormuz closed: US +65%, EU average +34%, UK +41% (week of Oct 19 vs week of Feb 23).

posts.text: Saudi Arabia contained a fire near Ras Tanura, its top export terminal, after an unclaimed attack; damage unclear. Houthis also claim new strikes on the East-West pipeline and Riyadh's airport, unconfirmed. Brent near $114.88; diesel $6.28/gal.

No official confirmation yet on the extent of Tuesday's Ras Tanura fire or the Houthis' pipeline and airport claims. Brent firmed to about $114.80 and TTF gas hit a fresh 2026 high above €97/MWh. US diesel: $6.35/gal.

Ghawar, in Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province near Ras Tanura, is the world's largest conventional oil field: ~3.8 million b/d across 280 km, discovered 1948. Its spare capacity makes Saudi Arabia OPEC+'s swing producer.
